M01.A01.description: Add a new person to contacts, such as an existing customer or someone you already deal with. For a new prospect, use Create lead instead.

M01.A02.description: Open one contact's full profile, showing details, owner, tags, communication preferences and relationships.

M01.A03.description: Find contacts by name, email, phone, company, owner, tag or creation date. Prospects are separate; use Search leads for those.

M01.A04.description: Change a contact's name, email, phone or company. Owner, preferences and relationships are handled by their own actions.

M01.A05.description: Archive a contact so it is hidden from searches and read-only, but kept with its history. Open tasks about them stay as they are.

M01.A06.description: Merge a duplicate contact into the one to keep, moving tags, relationships, tasks, deals and missing details over. The duplicate is marked merged.

M01.A07.description: Make a staff user the owner of a contact. For leads, use Assign lead owner instead.

M01.A08.description: Set how a contact may be reached by email, SMS or call, or turn on do not disturb to block all channels. Only the given channels change.

M01.A09.description: Link two contacts with a relationship such as spouse, colleague, manager or referred by. The other contact gets the matching link back.

M01.A10.description: Show everything that happened with a contact, newest first: changes, tasks, deals and the lead they came from.

M02.A01.description: Creates a new company record for a business account with its name and basic details. Use it to add an organization, not an individual person.

M02.A02.description: Opens one company record and shows its full profile and details. Use when you already know which company you want to look at.

M02.A03.description: Finds companies by name, domain, industry or other criteria and returns a list of matches. Use when you don't know the exact company.

M02.A04.description: Edits the information stored on an existing company, such as name, website, phone, address or industry. It does not change linked contacts or the account manager.

M02.A05.description: Archives a company so it is hidden from active lists but not permanently deleted. Different from merging duplicates, which combines two companies into one.

M02.A06.description: Connects an existing contact to a company so the person appears as part of that organization. The opposite of unlinking.

M02.A07.description: Removes the connection between a contact and a company, keeping both records. Use when a person leaves or was linked by mistake.

M02.A08.description: Sets which team member is responsible for a company account as its account manager. Differs from assigning a contact owner, which applies to a person record.

M02.A09.description: Combines two duplicate company records into a single one, keeping the merged data and linked contacts. Different from archive, which only hides one company.

M02.A10.description: Lists all contacts linked to a given company, showing the people who work there.

M03.A01.description: Adds a new lead, a prospect who is interested but not yet a customer. For an existing customer or someone you already deal with, create a contact instead.

M03.A02.description: Shows everything about one lead: source, status, score, owner, qualification answers and what it was converted into.

M03.A03.description: Finds leads (prospects, not yet customers) by creation date, source, status, owner or score. Dates are inclusive. Use it to browse many leads, not open one.

M03.A04.description: Edits a lead's name, email, phone or company, or marks it as contacted. Owner, source, score and qualification are changed with their own actions.

M03.A05.description: Makes a staff user the owner of a lead, responsible for following it up. For contacts, use assign contact owner instead.

M03.A06.description: Corrects where a lead came from (facebook_ads, google_ads, website, referral, event, manual), optionally with the campaign that brought them in.

M03.A07.description: Saves a lead's answers to the qualification questions (budget, authority, need, timeline). Only given answers change; markQualified needs all four answered.

M03.A08.description: Sets a lead's score from 0 to 100, or raises or lowers it by an amount (e.g. +10 after a demo). The result stays between 0 and 100.

M03.A09.description: Disqualifies a lead that won't buy and records why (no_budget, no_need, bad_timing, unreachable, competitor, spam, other). Not the same as converting it.

M03.A10.description: Converts a qualified lead into a customer: links or creates the contact with the same email and opens a deal at the pipeline's first stage. The lead needs an owner.

M04.A01.description: Open a new deal for a contact in a pipeline, with its value in USD. It starts at the first stage unless you pick one. To turn a qualified lead into a deal, use Convert lead instead.

M04.A02.description: Show everything about one deal: contact, owner, value, current stage and win probability, expected close date and status.

M04.A03.description: Find deals by contact, owner, stage, value range, expected close date range or name. Returns open deals unless a status is given.

M04.A04.description: Change the dollar value of an open deal, for example after a revised quote or scope change.

M04.A05.description: Move an open deal to another stage of its pipeline, such as Qualified, Proposal or Negotiation. To close it, use Mark won or Mark lost instead.

M04.A06.description: Make a staff user the owner of an open deal. Reassigns responsibility for the deal only, not for contacts or leads.

M04.A07.description: Set the date an open deal is expected to close. The date can't be in the past.

M04.A08.description: Close an open deal as won, meaning the sale was made.

M04.A09.description: Close an open deal as lost and record why, such as a competitor win or no budget. It can be reopened later.

M04.A10.description: Reopen a won or lost deal so it returns to the pipeline at the stage where it closed.

M05.A01.description: Creates a new sales pipeline with a name so deals can be tracked through stages. Use to set up a brand-new pipeline, not to add a stage to an existing one.

M05.A02.description: Shows the full setup of one pipeline, including its stages, their order and win probabilities. Use to inspect a single pipeline rather than list all of them.
synonyms: how likely a deal is to close at each stage

M05.A03.description: Lists all sales pipelines available in the account, with their names. Use to browse or find a pipeline; for one pipeline's stages use Get pipeline configuration.

M05.A04.description: Changes the name of an existing pipeline. Does not touch its stages; to rename a stage use Rename pipeline stage.

M05.A05.description: Archives a pipeline so it is no longer used for new deals while keeping its history. It hides the pipeline rather than deleting it.

M05.A06.description: Adds a new stage to a pipeline, such as a new step in the sales process. Use to extend a pipeline, not to rename an existing stage.

M05.A07.description: Changes the name of an existing stage within a pipeline. The stage keeps its position and deals; to rename the whole pipeline use Rename pipeline.

M05.A08.description: Changes the order of the stages in a pipeline, moving them earlier or later in the sequence. It does not move any deals between stages.

M05.A09.description: Removes a stage from a pipeline, only if it has no deals in it. Use to clean up unused stages.

M05.A10.description: Sets the percent chance of winning for deals in a given stage, used for forecasting. It changes the stage rule, not any single opportunity's value.

M06.A01.description: Create a new to-do for a staff user, optionally linked to a contact, lead or opportunity. Add a due date only if one was given; it can't be in the past.

M06.A02.description: Show the full details of a single task: who it's assigned to, due date, priority, status and the record it relates to.

M06.A03.description: Find tasks by assignee, status, priority, due date range, overdue, linked record or title text. Returns open tasks unless a status is given.

M06.A04.description: Rewrite the title and/or description text of an open task. Doesn't change owner, due date or priority.

M06.A05.description: Give an open task to a staff user, or take it away from the current owner. Use it to reassign work.

M06.A06.description: Set or change the deadline of an open task. The date can't be in the past.

M06.A07.description: Set how important an open task is: low, normal, high or urgent.

M06.A08.description: Mark an open task as done because the work is finished. For tasks no longer needed, use Cancel task instead.

M06.A09.description: Bring a completed or cancelled task back to open. If its due date has passed, give a new date or it will show as overdue.

M06.A10.description: Cancel an open task that is no longer needed; it stays on record as cancelled. For finished work use Mark task complete instead.

M07.A01.description: Write a new note on a contact, lead, deal, appointment or invoice, such as what was said on a call. For a to-do with a due date, create a task instead.

M07.A02.description: Open a single note to read its text, author, the records it's attached to and whether it is pinned.

M07.A03.description: Find notes on a record, or by author, pinned status, date written or text. Pinned notes appear first, then newest. Differs from Get note, which opens one known note.

M07.A04.description: Rewrite the text of an existing note. The earlier wording is saved in the note's revision history.

M07.A05.description: Permanently delete a note along with its history. To only remove it from one record while keeping it, detach it instead.

M07.A06.description: Put an existing note on one more record (contact, lead, deal, appointment or invoice) so it shows in several places. Does not create a new note.

M07.A07.description: Take a note off one record while the note itself is kept. To remove the note entirely, use delete instead.

M07.A08.description: Pin a note so it appears at the top of the notes on its records.

M07.A09.description: Unpin a note that was pinned, so it goes back to normal date order among the notes.

M07.A10.description: Show every earlier version of a note's text, oldest first, ending with the current version. Useful to see who changed what.

M08.A01.description: Add a brand new tag to the account's tag list, optionally with a color and description. It doesn't put the tag on anyone; use Apply tag to record for that.

M08.A02.description: Show the account's tags in alphabetical order, optionally narrowed by part of the name or by color. Use it to see which tags exist.

M08.A03.description: Change the name of an existing tag. Every contact and lead that already has it shows the new name automatically.

M08.A04.description: Change the color of a tag. Only the look changes, not the name or the records using it.

M08.A05.description: Delete a tag nobody uses anymore. A tag still on records must first be removed from them or merged into another tag.

M08.A06.description: Put an existing tag on a contact or lead. The tag must already exist; this doesn't create new tags.

M08.A07.description: Take a tag off a contact or lead. The tag itself stays in the tag list and on other records.

M08.A08.description: List the contacts and leads that carry a given tag. For contacts with extra filters as well, use Search contacts with tag instead.

M08.A09.description: Combine two tags: everything with the source tag gets the target tag, then the source tag is deleted. Handy for duplicates.

M08.A10.description: Show how many contacts and leads use each tag, most used first, including tags with zero use. Good for spotting tags to clean up.

M09.A01.description: Creates a new smart list, a saved dynamic audience that automatically collects records matching a set of filter rules. Use it to start a new segment from scratch.

M09.A02.description: Shows the saved definition of one smart list, including its name and filter rules. It doesn't list matching records; use Preview for that.

M09.A03.description: Lists all saved smart lists so you can browse or find one by name. Returns the lists themselves, not the records inside them.

M09.A04.description: Changes the name of an existing smart list without touching its filter rules or contents.

M09.A05.description: Edits the filter rules of a smart list so it matches a different set of records. Use Rename instead to change only the name.

M09.A06.description: Shows a sample of the records that currently match a smart list's filters, so you can check the rules before relying on them. Use Count for just the total.

M09.A07.description: Returns only the number of records that currently match a smart list, without showing them. Use Preview to see the actual records.

M09.A08.description: Exports the records matching a smart list to a downloadable file such as a CSV, for use outside the CRM.

M09.A09.description: Makes a copy of an existing smart list with the same filter rules, so you can tweak it without changing the original.

M09.A10.description: Permanently removes a smart list and its saved filters. The records that matched it are not deleted.

M10.A01.description: Creates a new custom field with a name and data type (text, number, date, dropdown) on a module such as contacts or companies, to store extra business data.

M10.A02.description: Shows the full definition of one custom field: its type, label, help text, validation rules and dropdown options. Use for a single field; to see all fields use the list action.

M10.A03.description: Lists all custom fields defined for a chosen module, such as contacts, leads or companies. Use to browse available fields rather than inspect one.

M10.A04.description: Changes the display label of an existing custom field without altering its type, values or validation. It does not edit the help text.

M10.A05.description: Updates the help text or hint shown to users beside a custom field. It leaves the field label and validation unchanged.

M10.A06.description: Sets the rules a custom field value must meet, such as required, minimum or maximum, length or pattern, so bad data is rejected.

M10.A07.description: Adds a new choice to a dropdown custom field so users can select it. To hide an existing choice instead, use retire option.

M10.A08.description: Retires a dropdown option so it can no longer be chosen for new records, while keeping existing values. Differs from adding an option or archiving the whole field.

M10.A09.description: Sets or changes the value of a custom field on a specific record, such as a contact or company. It fills in data rather than changing the field definition.

M10.A10.description: Archives a custom field so it is hidden and no longer used, while keeping stored data. Differs from retiring a single dropdown option.

M11.A01.description: Open a single conversation to see who it is with, its status and owner, and every SMS and email exchanged, oldest first. For counts and a recap, use Summarize conversation history instead.

M11.A02.description: Find conversations by contact or lead, owner, open or closed, unread, channel, or last message date, newest activity first. To find who is waiting for a reply, use List unanswered conversations.

M11.A03.description: Make a user responsible for answering a conversation. This does not change who owns the contact or lead record itself.

M11.A04.description: Mark a conversation as read so it no longer shows as having new messages. The opposite of Mark conversation unread.

M11.A05.description: Mark a conversation as unread so it shows up again as needing attention. The opposite of Mark conversation read.

M11.A06.description: Close a conversation that needs nothing more. A new message from the person reopens it automatically.

M11.A07.description: Reopen a conversation that was closed so it is active again, without waiting for a new message from the person.

M11.A08.description: Leave an internal comment on a conversation for teammates; the customer never sees it. To message the customer, send an SMS or email instead.

M11.A09.description: Sum up a conversation: message counts each way and by channel, start date, last message each way, and who is waiting on whom.

M11.A10.description: List open conversations waiting for a reply, longest wait first, either where the customer wrote last or where we did. People never messaged do not appear.

M12.A01.description: Write a text message to a contact or lead and save it as a draft without sending it. Use Send SMS later to deliver it.

M12.A02.description: Check how a text would be split and billed: character count, encoding (GSM-7 or UCS-2 for emoji) and number of segments. Nothing is sent.

M12.A03.description: Send a text message right now, either a saved draft or a new message to a contact or lead. Refused if they opted out or have no valid mobile.

M12.A04.description: Schedule a text message to go out at a later time, from a saved draft or a new message. Same consent rules as sending now.

M12.A05.description: Cancel a scheduled text message before it goes out, so it is not delivered.

M12.A06.description: Open one text message to see who it is to or from, the text, its status and timestamps.

M12.A07.description: Find text messages by contact or lead, direction, status, date or text content. Results are newest first.

M12.A08.description: Check whether a text message was delivered and, if it failed, the reason why.

M12.A09.description: Simulate a text arriving from a phone number, as if the person replied. It lands in their conversation as unread; STOP-type replies also opt them out.

M12.A10.description: Record that a contact or lead no longer wants text messages, so future sends to their number are refused. For email use Record email unsubscribe.

M13.A01.description: Write an email to a contact or lead and save it as a draft without sending. Can also draft a payment reminder for an open invoice. Send it later with Send email.

M13.A02.description: Show a draft email as it would go out and list anything that would block it, such as unsubscribed, do-not-disturb, missing address or a recent reminder. Does not send.

M13.A03.description: Send an email right now, either a saved draft or a new message to a contact or lead. Refused if they unsubscribed or opted out. Use Schedule email for later.

M13.A04.description: Schedule an email to go out at a later date and time, from a saved draft or a new message. Same consent rules as sending. Use Send email for immediate delivery.

M13.A05.description: Cancel an email that is scheduled but not yet sent, so it will not go out. Does not unsend emails already delivered.

M13.A06.description: Open one email to see who it's to or from, subject, body, kind, status and timestamps. Use Search email messages to find emails first.

M13.A07.description: Find emails by contact or lead, invoice, campaign, kind, direction, status, date or text, newest first. Use Get email details for a single known email.

M13.A08.description: Check whether an email was delivered or bounced, and the reason why. Use it to troubleshoot messages that did not arrive.

M13.A09.description: Simulate an email arriving from an address, as if the person replied. It appears in their conversation as unread. For testing, not for sending.

M13.A10.description: Record that a contact or lead unsubscribed from email, so marketing and follow-up emails are refused while invoices still go out. For texts, use the SMS opt-out.

M14.A01.description: Creates a new reusable email or SMS template with a name and body content. Use it to start a template from scratch; to copy an existing one use Duplicate template.

M14.A02.description: Opens a single message template by its id and shows its name, content, variables and status. Use Search templates when you don't know which one.

M14.A03.description: Finds message templates by name, keyword, channel or status. Use it to browse or locate templates when you don't have the exact one.

M14.A04.description: Edits the subject or body text of an existing template, saving the change as a new version. Doesn't create a copy or roll back to an older version.

M14.A05.description: Archives a template so it is no longer offered for new messages, without permanently deleting it. Different from Restore template version, which rolls back content.

M14.A06.description: Makes a copy of an existing template under a new name so you can tweak it without changing the original. Different from Create, which starts blank.

M14.A07.description: Declares the merge variables (placeholders like first name or company) a template can use, including names and default values. Doesn't check them; Validate does that.

M14.A08.description: Checks that every variable used in the template text is defined and correctly written, reporting missing or unknown placeholders. It doesn't change the template.

M14.A09.description: Shows how a template looks with sample data filled into its variables, so you can preview the final message without sending anything.

M14.A10.description: Rolls a template back to a previously saved version of its content. Different from Update content, which writes new text.

M15.A01.description: Creates a new draft marketing campaign with a name and main channel (email or SMS). Audience and message steps are added afterwards, before launching.

M15.A02.description: Shows everything about one campaign: status, audience and size, steps, schedule and leads generated. For sending results use campaign performance instead.

M15.A03.description: Lists campaigns, optionally filtered by status, channel or name, to find or browse existing outreach.

M15.A04.description: Chooses who a draft or scheduled campaign is sent to: everyone with a tag, specific contacts, or both. Does not change message content or timing.

M15.A05.description: Adds a message to a draft or scheduled campaign with channel, subject (email), body and the number of days after launch it goes out.

M15.A06.description: Sets the start date and time of a draft campaign, making it scheduled, or clears it to return to draft. Different from launching now.

M15.A07.description: Launches a draft or scheduled campaign immediately, sending day-0 steps to reachable contacts. Opted-out and do-not-disturb people are skipped and counted.

M15.A08.description: Pauses an active campaign so no further steps are sent. Use resume to continue it later.

M15.A09.description: Resumes a paused campaign so its remaining steps continue to go out.

M15.A10.description: Shows how a campaign is doing: messages sent, delivered, bounced or failed, replies and leads generated. For setup details use get campaign details.

M16.A01.description: Creates a new, empty automation workflow with a name so steps can be added afterward. Use it to start a new automation, not to edit an existing one.

M16.A02.description: Shows the full definition of one workflow, including its steps, order and current status. Use it to inspect a single automation rather than list all.

M16.A03.description: Lists the workflows in the account with their names and statuses, so you can browse or find an automation. Does not show steps of one workflow.

M16.A04.description: Adds a new step, such as an action, wait or condition, to a workflow. Use it to extend an automation, unlike editing or deleting an existing step.

M16.A05.description: Changes the settings or content of an existing step in a workflow, such as its action, delay or condition. Does not add or delete steps.

M16.A06.description: Deletes a single step from a workflow so it no longer runs. Use it to take out a step, not to pause or delete the whole workflow.

M16.A07.description: Checks a workflow for errors such as missing settings or broken step order, without publishing it. Run it before going live.

M16.A08.description: Makes a workflow live so it starts running for contacts. Use it to activate a draft or resume after changes; the opposite of Pause workflow.

M16.A09.description: Temporarily stops a live workflow from running without deleting it or its steps. Differs from Publish, which turns it on.

M16.A10.description: Shows the past runs of a workflow, including which contacts went through it and whether steps succeeded or failed. Useful for troubleshooting.

M17.A01.description: Creates a new event trigger that listens for a chosen kind of event and starts automation. Use it to set up a trigger from scratch, not to change an existing one.

M17.A02.description: Shows the full setup of one trigger: its event type, conditions, linked workflow and whether it is on. Use it to inspect a single trigger.

M17.A03.description: Lists all event triggers in the account with their basic status, so you can browse or find one. For one trigger's full setup, use Get trigger configuration.

M17.A04.description: Changes which kind of event a trigger reacts to, such as form submitted or appointment booked. Does not edit the filter conditions.

M17.A05.description: Edits the conditions or filters a trigger checks before it fires, such as only for certain tags or sources. Does not change the event type.

M17.A06.description: Connects a trigger to a workflow so the workflow runs whenever the trigger fires. Use it to link or change the workflow a trigger starts.

M17.A07.description: Turns a trigger on so it starts reacting to incoming events and launching its workflow. The opposite of Disable trigger.

M17.A08.description: Turns a trigger off so it stops firing and starting workflows, without deleting it. The opposite of Enable trigger.

M17.A09.description: Runs a trigger against a made-up sample event to check whether its conditions match and the workflow would start. Nothing real is affected.

M17.A10.description: Shows the past record of when a trigger fired, with times and outcomes. Use it to see whether and why a trigger ran.

M18.A01.description: Creates a new empty form with a name so you can then add fields to it. Use before adding fields; it does not publish the form.

M18.A02.description: Shows the full definition of a form: its fields, order, validation rules and publish state. Use to inspect one form, unlike listing all forms.

M18.A03.description: Lists the forms that exist in the account, with names and status. Use to browse or find a form; for one form's fields use Get form definition.

M18.A04.description: Adds a new field, such as a text box, email or dropdown, to an existing form. Use for new fields; to change an existing one use Update form field.

M18.A05.description: Changes an existing field on a form, such as its label, type, placeholder or required setting. Does not add new fields or change their order.

M18.A06.description: Changes the order in which fields appear on a form. Use to move fields up or down; it does not edit field content.

M18.A07.description: Sets rules that submitted answers must meet, like required fields, formats or length limits. Applies to the whole form's validation, not field content or layout.

M18.A08.description: Makes a form live so people can fill it out. Use once the fields and rules are ready; it does not collect responses itself.

M18.A09.description: Submits a test response to a form as if a visitor filled it in, for trying out the form. Creates a submission record.

M18.A10.description: Lists the responses people have submitted to a form. Use to review collected answers; not for form structure or fields.

M19.A01.description: Creates a new survey with a name and purpose so questions can be added afterwards. Starts as an unpublished draft, not yet visible to respondents.

M19.A02.description: Shows the full setup of one survey: its questions, order, branching rules and status. Use it to inspect a survey, not to see answers.

M19.A03.description: Lists existing surveys with their status such as draft, published or closed. Use it to browse or find a survey before opening it.

M19.A04.description: Adds a new question to a survey, such as multiple choice, rating or free text. Use Update question to change an existing one.

M19.A05.description: Edits an existing survey question, such as its wording, type, options or required setting. Use Add question to create a new one instead.

M19.A06.description: Defines skip logic so the next question shown depends on a respondent's answer. Controls the flow between questions, not their content.

M19.A07.description: Makes a draft survey live so respondents can answer it. Opposite of Close survey, which stops collecting answers.

M19.A08.description: Stops a survey from accepting new responses while keeping existing answers. Opposite of Publish survey.

M19.A09.description: Creates a test survey response with made-up answers to try out the flow and branching. Does not come from a real respondent.

M19.A10.description: Shows aggregated results for a survey, like response counts and answer breakdowns per question. Gives totals rather than the survey setup.

M20.A01.description: Creates a new calendar used for taking appointment bookings, with a name and basic details. Use to set up a new bookable calendar from scratch.

M20.A02.description: Shows the full settings of one calendar, including timezone, host, appointment duration, buffer and visibility. Use to review how a calendar is configured.

M20.A03.description: Lists all calendars available, so you can browse or find one to open. Does not change anything or show appointments.

M20.A04.description: Edits general calendar details such as name and description. For timezone, host, duration, buffer or visibility use the dedicated setting actions instead.

M20.A05.description: Sets the timezone a calendar uses for its working hours and booking times. Use when a calendar shows the wrong local time.

M20.A06.description: Assigns the user who hosts a calendar and takes its bookings. Differs from assigning a host to a single existing appointment.

M20.A07.description: Sets how long appointments booked on a calendar last, such as 30 or 60 minutes. Applies to new bookings on that calendar.

M20.A08.description: Sets the buffer time kept free before or after appointments on a calendar so bookings are not back to back.

M20.A09.description: Sets whether a calendar is public or private, controlling who can see and book it. Not the same as publishing a booking page.

M20.A10.description: Archives a calendar that is no longer used so it stops taking bookings, without permanently deleting it.

M21.A01.description: Book a new appointment with a contact or lead, hosted by a user, at a future time. Defaults to 30 minutes; refused if the host is busy or unavailable.

M21.A02.description: Open one appointment to see who it's with, host, attendees, time, location, status and outcome.

M21.A03.description: Find appointments by contact or lead, host, status or date range, soonest first. Use it to check whether someone has a meeting booked.

M21.A04.description: Move a booked appointment to a new future time, keeping its length unless a new duration or end time is given. Not the same as cancelling.

M21.A05.description: Cancel a booked appointment, with an optional reason. Use it when the meeting won't happen at all, rather than moving it or marking it done.

M21.A06.description: Hand a booked appointment over to a different host. Refused if the new host is unavailable or busy at that time.

M21.A07.description: Invite another contact, lead or teammate to a booked appointment as an additional attendee.

M21.A08.description: Remove an invited attendee, other than the main contact or lead, from a booked appointment.

M21.A09.description: Record that the contact or lead didn't show up to an appointment that has already started. Differs from completed, where the meeting happened.

M21.A10.description: Mark an appointment that has started as completed, with an optional outcome note. Differs from no-show or cancel.

M22.A01.description: Define the recurring weekly working hours for a calendar or user, such as Monday to Friday 9 to 5. Replaces the regular schedule, unlike date-specific availability which only affects one day.

M22.A02.description: Show the current recurring weekly working hours for a calendar or user. Read-only view of the regular schedule, does not change anything.

M22.A03.description: Add availability for one specific date that differs from the weekly schedule, like opening on a holiday or extra hours on a Saturday. Use Block time range to remove time instead.

M22.A04.description: Remove a previously added date-specific availability so that day goes back to the regular weekly hours. Does not remove blocked time.

M22.A05.description: Block a time range so it can't be booked, for example lunch, vacation or a meeting. Differs from date-specific availability, which adds open time.

M22.A06.description: Remove an existing blocked time range so that time becomes bookable again. Does not delete appointments.

M22.A07.description: Set how much advance notice is required before a booking, such as at least 24 hours. Differs from maximum booking horizon, which limits how far ahead people can book.

M22.A08.description: Set how far into the future people can book, such as 60 days ahead. Differs from minimum booking notice, which sets the shortest lead time.

M22.A09.description: Find open bookable time slots for a calendar or user over a date range, based on working hours, blocks and existing appointments.

M22.A10.description: Check whether a proposed time clashes with existing appointments, blocks or working hours. Only reports conflicts, does not book or change anything.

M23.A01.description: Creates a new public booking page where customers can schedule appointments. Use it to start a fresh page; to change an existing one use Update booking page content.

M23.A02.description: Shows the full settings of one booking page, including its linked calendar, intake fields, confirmation message, redirect and published state.

M23.A03.description: Lists all booking pages, so you can browse them and see which are published or drafts. Use Get booking page for one page's details.

M23.A04.description: Edits the visible content of a booking page such as its title, headline and description text. Does not change calendar, intake fields or confirmation message.

M23.A05.description: Connects a calendar to a booking page so bookings are made against that calendar's availability and host.

M23.A06.description: Defines the questions and fields visitors must fill in when booking, like name, phone or custom questions on the booking page.

M23.A07.description: Sets the message shown to visitors after they successfully book, such as thank-you text or instructions. Differs from the redirect URL, which sends them elsewhere.

M23.A08.description: Sets a web address where visitors are sent after booking instead of seeing the confirmation message on the page.

M23.A09.description: Makes a booking page live so the public can open it and book appointments. Opposite of Unpublish booking page.

M23.A10.description: Takes a booking page offline so the public can no longer book through it, keeping its settings. Opposite of Publish booking page.

M24.A01.description: Creates a new event such as a workshop, webinar or group session with its title, date and location. Use this to set up a session before anyone registers.

M24.A02.description: Shows the full details of one event, including date, location, capacity and registration counts. Use it to look at a single known event rather than searching many.

M24.A03.description: Finds events by name, date, status or other filters and returns a list of matches. Use it when you don't have the event yet.

M24.A04.description: Changes general event information such as title, description, date, time or location. For changing only the number of seats, use Set event capacity instead.

M24.A05.description: Sets the maximum number of attendees an event can hold. Use it to raise or lower seats; it doesn't edit other event details.

M24.A06.description: Registers a contact as an attendee of an event, taking one seat. If the event is full, use Add attendee to waitlist instead.

M24.A07.description: Cancels an attendee's registration for an event and frees their seat. It removes the registration, not the event itself.

M24.A08.description: Puts a contact on an event's waitlist when it is full, without giving them a seat. Later use Promote waitlisted attendee to confirm them.

M24.A09.description: Moves a waitlisted attendee into a confirmed registration when a seat opens up. Differs from Register attendee, which is for people not on the waitlist.

M24.A10.description: Marks a registered attendee as present at the event on arrival. Use it on the day of the event, not for registering.

M25.A01.description: Creates a new product in the catalog that can be sold, with its name, description and basic details. Use before adding prices or variants.

M25.A02.description: Shows the full details of one product, including its name, description, status, variants and SKU. Use when you already know which product.

M25.A03.description: Finds products in the catalog by name, SKU, status or other filters and returns a list of matches. Use when the product is not known yet.

M25.A04.description: Edits a product's general information such as name, description or category. Does not change variants, SKU or stock, which have their own actions.

M25.A05.description: Archives a product so it is no longer offered or shown for sale, while keeping its history. Differs from editing details; it retires the whole product.

M25.A06.description: Adds a new variant to an existing product, such as a different size, color or option, so it can be sold separately.

M25.A07.description: Changes an existing variant of a product, such as its name, options or attributes. Differs from adding a new variant or editing the parent product.

M25.A08.description: Sets or changes the SKU code that identifies a product or variant for inventory and tracking purposes.

M25.A09.description: Sets the stock quantity on hand for a product or variant, for example after a count or restock. Differs from only checking availability.

M25.A10.description: Checks how much of a product or variant is currently in stock and available to sell. Read-only; does not change the quantity.

M26.A01.description: Creates a new price for a product, with amount, currency and billing type. Use it to add a price option; to change an existing price use the specific Set actions.

M26.A02.description: Shows the full details of one price, including amount, currency, billing interval, trial and whether it is the default or archived.

M26.A03.description: Lists all prices attached to a product, so you can see its pricing options. Differs from product search, which finds products rather than their prices.

M26.A04.description: Changes the display name or label of an existing price, such as 'Monthly' or 'Annual Pro'. Does not alter the amount or billing terms.

M26.A05.description: Sets or changes how much a price costs. Use it to raise, lower or correct the amount; currency and interval are changed separately.

M26.A06.description: Sets the currency a price is charged in, such as USD, EUR or GBP. The amount and billing interval stay unchanged.

M26.A07.description: Sets how often a price bills, such as one-time, monthly, quarterly or yearly. Use it to turn a price into recurring or one-off.

M26.A08.description: Sets the free trial length on a recurring price, in days, before billing begins. Differs from changing a subscription's trial end date.

M26.A09.description: Marks one price as the default for its product, used when no specific price is chosen. Replaces the previous default.

M26.A10.description: Archives a price so it can no longer be used for new sales, while keeping history and existing subscriptions intact.

M27.A01.description: Creates a new quote (proposal) for a customer, to which products and line items can then be added. Use it to start a fresh estimate before sending it.

M27.A02.description: Shows the full details of one quote, including its line items, totals, discount, expiry and current status.

M27.A03.description: Finds quotes by customer, status, date or number. Use it to browse or filter many quotes rather than opening a single known one.

M27.A04.description: Adds a product or service line to an existing quote with quantity and price. Differs from updating a line that is already on the quote.

M27.A05.description: Changes an existing line on a quote, such as its quantity, price or description. Use Add quote line item for new lines.

M27.A06.description: Sets or changes the date after which a quote is no longer valid for acceptance.

M27.A07.description: Applies a percentage or fixed-amount discount to a quote to lower its total. Applies to the quote itself, not to an order.

M27.A08.description: Sends the quote to the customer so they can review and accept it. Marks it as sent; it does not record their acceptance.

M27.A09.description: Records that the customer has accepted a sent quote. Use it once approval is received, before converting the quote to an invoice.

M27.A10.description: Turns an accepted quote into an invoice carrying over its line items and totals, ready to bill the customer.

M28.A01.description: Start a new draft invoice for a contact, optionally with line items, a due date and a memo. Nothing is sent to the customer until it is issued.

M28.A02.description: Open one invoice to see its contact, line items, total, amount paid and due, due date, days overdue, reminders sent and payments applied.

M28.A03.description: Find invoices by contact, status (draft, open, paid, void), date range, minimum amount due or invoice number. For just overdue ones ranked, use the overdue list instead.

M28.A04.description: Add a line item with description, quantity and unit price to a draft invoice; the total is recalculated automatically.

M28.A05.description: Edit a draft invoice: change its memo, switch which contact it is for, or replace all of its line items at once.

M28.A06.description: Set or move the due date of a draft or open invoice, for example to give a customer more time to pay.

M28.A07.description: Issue a draft invoice so it becomes open and is emailed to the contact; due date defaults to 30 days out. Different from just creating the draft.

M28.A08.description: Email the contact a payment reminder for an open invoice right away, at most once per 24 hours. To review the wording first, draft an email instead.

M28.A09.description: Void a draft or open invoice that has no payments, recording a reason. This cannot be undone; it differs from cancelling a payment request.

M28.A10.description: List open invoices past their due date, most overdue first, with days overdue, amount due and last reminder date. Simpler than a general invoice search.

M29.A01.description: Creates a payment link asking a contact to pay an amount, optionally tied to an open invoice, defaulting to the balance still due. It only makes the link; nothing is sent.

M29.A02.description: Looks up one payment request (link) to see who it's for, the amount, the invoice, and whether it's still pending, paid or cancelled.

M29.A03.description: Cancels a payment request that hasn't been paid so its link stops working. Use this for unpaid links, not for undoing payments already received.

M29.A04.description: Logs a payment from a contact as a simulated entry by card, bank transfer, cash or check, either succeeded or failed. Successful ones are applied to the related invoice, otherwise left unallocated.

M29.A05.description: Shows a single payment with its amount, method, whether it succeeded, and which invoices it was applied to.

M29.A06.description: Finds payments by contact, invoice, status, method or date range, or only those with money not yet applied to an invoice. Newest first; use to browse many payments.

M29.A07.description: Applies money from a succeeded payment to one of the same contact's open invoices, by default as much as fits. Use to settle an invoice with an unallocated payment.

M29.A08.description: Takes a payment back off an invoice, such as when it was applied to the wrong one. The invoice reopens and the money returns to unallocated.

M29.A09.description: Produces a receipt for a succeeded payment with receipt number, payer, amount, method, date and the invoices it paid.

M29.A10.description: Explains why a payment failed, such as declined card, insufficient funds, expired card or bank rejection, and suggests what to do next.

M30.A01.description: Starts a new recurring billing subscription for a customer on a chosen price or plan. Use it to sign someone up for ongoing billing.

M30.A02.description: Shows the full details of one subscription, such as plan, status, quantity, trial and next billing date.

M30.A03.description: Finds subscriptions by customer, status, plan or other filters. Use it to browse many subscriptions rather than open one known record.

M30.A04.description: Switches an existing subscription to a different plan or price, as an upgrade or downgrade. It does not change the number of seats.

M30.A05.description: Changes how many units or seats a subscription bills for. It keeps the same plan, unlike changing the plan.

M30.A06.description: Sets or changes the date when a subscription's free trial ends and billing begins. Use it to extend or shorten a trial.

M30.A07.description: Temporarily stops billing on a subscription without ending it. Use it to hold a subscription; Cancel ends it for good.

M30.A08.description: Restarts billing on a paused subscription so charges continue again. It only applies to subscriptions that were paused.

M30.A09.description: Ends a subscription so it stops renewing and billing. Use it for a permanent stop; Pause only holds billing temporarily.

M30.A10.description: Shows what the subscription's next invoice will look like, with amounts, proration and date, without creating or charging anything.

M31.A01.description: Creates a new coupon with a code and discount so customers can get a promotion. Use it to start a coupon from scratch, not to change an existing one.

M31.A02.description: Shows the full details of one coupon, including its code, discount, validity dates, limits and status. Use when you already know which coupon you want.

M31.A03.description: Finds coupons by code, name, status or other filters and returns a list of matches. Use when you don't know the exact coupon.

M31.A04.description: Changes the descriptive text of a coupon, such as its internal explanation or label. It does not change the discount amount or dates.

M31.A05.description: Sets or changes how much a coupon takes off, as a percentage or fixed amount. Use for the discount size, not for dates or usage limits.

M31.A06.description: Sets the start and end dates when a coupon can be used. Use for validity period, not for how many times it can be redeemed.

M31.A07.description: Sets the maximum number of times a coupon can be redeemed, in total or per customer. Use for usage caps, not for dates.

M31.A08.description: Limits a coupon so it only applies to selected products. Use to narrow which items qualify for the discount.

M31.A09.description: Checks whether a coupon code can be used on a particular order and what discount it would give, without applying it. Differs from applying a coupon to the order.

M31.A10.description: Turns a coupon off so it can no longer be redeemed. The coupon record stays for history, unlike deleting it.

M32.A01.description: Starts a new draft order for a contact that can still be edited before it is submitted. Use it to begin a purchase, not to add items to an existing one.

M32.A02.description: Shows the full details of one order, including items, totals, shipping address, coupon and current status. Use when you already know which order.

M32.A03.description: Finds orders by customer, status, date or order number and returns a list of matches. Use when you don't have the exact order.

M32.A04.description: Adds a product or price as a new line on a draft order. To change how many of an existing item, use Update order quantity instead.

M32.A05.description: Changes the quantity of an item already on an order. Use it to increase or decrease amounts; to add a new product use Add order line item.

M32.A06.description: Sets or changes the delivery address where an order will be shipped.

M32.A07.description: Applies a coupon or discount code to an order so the discount reduces its total. Does not create or validate the coupon itself.

M32.A08.description: Submits a draft order to finalize and place it, so it is no longer a draft. Use after items, address and coupon are set.

M32.A09.description: Cancels an order so it will not be processed or fulfilled. Different from Mark order fulfilled, which closes a delivered order, and from refunds for money back.

M32.A10.description: Marks an order as fulfilled once the goods or services have been delivered. Different from Cancel order, which stops it.

M33.A01.description: Start a new refund request for a recorded payment, asking to return money to a customer. It begins the process; approval and the actual refund happen in later steps.

M33.A02.description: Open one refund request and see its amount, reason, status and linked payment. Use Search refund requests when you don't know the exact one.

M33.A03.description: Find refund requests by filters like status, customer, payment or date. Returns a list, unlike Get refund request which opens one known request.

M33.A04.description: Set or change the reason given for a refund request, such as damaged item or duplicate charge. Does not change the amount or approval status.

M33.A05.description: Set a partial amount to refund instead of the full payment. Use it when only part of the money should go back to the customer.

M33.A06.description: Check how much of a payment can still be refunded after earlier refunds. A read-only check that changes nothing.

M33.A07.description: Approve a pending refund request so it can be paid out. Approving does not move money; use Execute simulated refund afterward. Opposite of Reject.

M33.A08.description: Reject a pending refund request so no money is returned. Opposite of Approve refund request; the request is closed as declined.

M33.A09.description: Carry out an approved refund as a simulated payout back to the customer. Requires approval first; no real money moves.

M33.A10.description: Check whether an executed refund has gone through, is pending or failed. Differs from Get refund request, which shows the request itself.

M34.A01.description: Creates a new tax rule with a name, rate and region so it can be applied to simulated sales. Use it to start a rule from scratch.

M34.A02.description: Shows the full details of one tax rule, including its rate, region, category and inclusive setting. Use it to look at a single rule, not browse all.

M34.A03.description: Lists all configured tax rules so you can browse or compare them. Use it to see every rule, rather than opening a single one.

M34.A04.description: Changes the percentage rate charged by an existing tax rule. Use it when the tax percentage changes, not the region or category.

M34.A05.description: Sets the country, state or region where a tax rule applies. Use it to change where the tax is charged, not how much.

M34.A06.description: Assigns a tax category to a product so the right tax rule applies to it. Use it to classify an item for tax purposes.

M34.A07.description: Switches a tax rule between tax-inclusive pricing (tax already in the price) and tax-exclusive pricing (tax added on top).

M34.A08.description: Records that a customer is exempt from tax, such as with a resale or nonprofit certificate. Applies to the customer, not to a rule.

M34.A09.description: Calculates the tax amount for an order using the active tax rules and any customer exemptions. It only computes the result and changes no rule.

M34.A10.description: Turns off a tax rule so it is no longer applied to new sales, while keeping it on record.

M35.A01.description: Creates a new website to hold pages, navigation and SEO settings. Use it to start a brand-new site, not to add a page to an existing one.

M35.A02.description: Shows the settings of one website, such as its name, home page, navigation, SEO defaults and published state.

M35.A03.description: Lists all websites in the account so you can browse or pick one. Use it to see every site rather than the details of a single site.

M35.A04.description: Changes the name of an existing website. It does not change the pages, navigation or published state.

M35.A05.description: Adds a new page to a website's page collection. Different from creating a landing page or a blog post, which are standalone content records.

M35.A06.description: Chooses which existing page of the website is the home page, shown when visitors open the main address.

M35.A07.description: Edits the website's navigation menu, such as which pages appear and in what order.

M35.A08.description: Sets the default SEO values for the whole website, such as title pattern and meta description. For one page's SEO, use the landing page or blog post SEO actions.

M35.A09.description: Makes the website live and visible to visitors. Reverse of unpublishing the site.

M35.A10.description: Takes the website offline so visitors can no longer see it, keeping its content. Reverse of publishing the site.

M36.A01.description: Creates a new sales funnel, an ordered journey of steps that leads visitors toward a conversion. Use it to start a funnel from scratch before adding steps.

M36.A02.description: Shows the full definition of one funnel: its steps in order, linked pages, goal and publish state. Use to inspect a single funnel rather than list all.

M36.A03.description: Lists all funnels with their basic info and status. Use to browse or find a funnel; for one funnel's full steps use the definition view.

M36.A04.description: Adds a new step to a funnel, such as an opt-in, sales or thank-you stage, at the end or a chosen position.

M36.A05.description: Changes the order of existing steps in a funnel so visitors move through them in a new sequence. Does not add or delete steps.

M36.A06.description: Deletes a step from a funnel so it is no longer part of the journey. Other steps remain and close the gap.

M36.A07.description: Connects an existing landing page to a funnel step so that step shows that page to visitors. Different from attaching a form to a page.

M36.A08.description: Defines the conversion goal of a funnel, such as reaching a final step or completing a purchase, which is used to measure success.

M36.A09.description: Makes a funnel live so visitors can go through its steps. Use after steps, pages and goal are ready.

M36.A10.description: Shows conversion metrics for a funnel, such as visitors per step, drop-off and overall conversion rate. Read-only analytics.

M37.A01.description: Creates a new landing page for a campaign or offer. Use it to start a page from scratch; to edit an existing page use Update page content.

M37.A02.description: Opens one landing page and shows its content, sections, attached form and publish status. Use when you know which page you want to see.

M37.A03.description: Finds landing pages by name, status or keyword and returns a list of matches. Use when you don't have the exact page.

M37.A04.description: Edits the text, headline and body content of an existing landing page. It doesn't add new sections or change SEO details.

M37.A05.description: Adds a new content section, such as a hero, testimonial or call-to-action block, to a landing page. It doesn't change the order of existing sections.

M37.A06.description: Changes the order in which sections appear on a landing page, such as moving a block up or down.

M37.A07.description: Connects an existing form to a landing page so visitors can submit their details there. It doesn't create or edit the form itself.

M37.A08.description: Sets the search engine title, meta description and keywords for a landing page. Differs from Update page content, which changes visible text.

M37.A09.description: Makes a landing page live so visitors can reach it. Use Unpublish landing page to take it offline again.

M37.A10.description: Takes a live landing page offline so visitors can no longer see it, while keeping the page and its content saved.

M38.A01.description: Creates a new blog post as a draft with title and body. Use to start a fresh article; it is not published until you publish it.

M38.A02.description: Opens a single blog post and shows its title, content, author, categories and status. Use when you already know which post you want.

M38.A03.description: Finds blog posts by keyword, author, category or status. Use to browse or look up articles when you don't have the exact post.

M38.A04.description: Edits the title, body or other content of an existing blog post. Use for rewrites and corrections; SEO, author and categories have their own actions.

M38.A05.description: Sets or changes the author credited on a blog post. Different from editing the post content.

M38.A06.description: Sets the categories a blog post belongs to, for organizing articles by topic.

M38.A07.description: Sets the SEO title, meta description and related search metadata for a blog post.

M38.A08.description: Schedules a blog post to go live automatically at a future date and time. Unlike Publish post, it does not go live immediately.

M38.A09.description: Publishes a blog post immediately so it is visible to readers. Unlike Schedule post publication, it goes live now.

M38.A10.description: Takes a published blog post offline and returns it to draft, hiding it from readers without deleting it.

M39.A01.description: Uploads a new image or file to the media library so it can be used on pages, emails and sites. Creates a new asset rather than swapping an existing file.

M39.A02.description: Shows the details of a single media asset, such as its name, file type, size, folder, alt text and upload date. Use to inspect one known asset.

M39.A03.description: Finds media assets in the library by name, file type, folder or other filters. Use when you don't know which asset you need yet.

M39.A04.description: Changes the display name or filename of an existing media asset without touching the file itself or its location.

M39.A05.description: Sets or edits the alternative text of an image asset, used for accessibility and SEO. It does not change the asset name or file.

M39.A06.description: Moves a media asset into a different folder in the library to keep files organized. The file and name stay the same.

M39.A07.description: Swaps the file of an existing asset for a new version while keeping the same asset record and its links. Different from uploading a new asset.

M39.A08.description: Lists where a media asset is used, such as pages, emails, blog posts or courses. Check this before deleting or replacing a file.

M39.A09.description: Creates a link for opening or downloading a media asset, to share a file with someone outside the library.

M39.A10.description: Permanently deletes a media asset that isn't used anywhere. Refuses assets still referenced by pages or messages; for those, check references first.

M40.A01.description: Creates a new course (learning program) with a title and basic details. Use it to start a course from scratch; add sections and lessons afterwards.

M40.A02.description: Shows the full details of one course, including its title, description, status, instructor, sections and prerequisites. Use when you already know which course you want.

M40.A03.description: Finds courses by keyword, status or other filters and returns a list of matches. Use when you don't know the exact course.

M40.A04.description: Edits a course's main details such as title, description or cover info. Does not change sections, instructor, prerequisites or publish status, which have their own actions.

M40.A05.description: Adds a new section (module or chapter) to a course to group lessons. To change the order of existing sections, use Reorder course sections instead.

M40.A06.description: Changes the order in which a course's existing sections appear. Use it to rearrange chapters; it does not create or delete sections.

M40.A07.description: Assigns an instructor (teacher or trainer) to a course. Use it to set or change who leads the course.

M40.A08.description: Sets which other courses a learner must finish before taking this course. Use it to require earlier courses as prerequisites.

M40.A09.description: Publishes a course so learners can see and enroll in it. Different from Archive course, which retires it.

M40.A10.description: Archives a course so it is retired and no longer offered, while keeping its records. Different from Publish course, which makes it available.

M41.A01.description: Creates a new lesson in a course, with a title and optional content. Use it to add a brand-new lesson rather than editing an existing one.

M41.A02.description: Shows the full details of one lesson, including its content, media, schedule, completion rules and published state.

M41.A03.description: Finds lessons by title, course, section or status. Use it to look up lessons when you don't have the exact one.

M41.A04.description: Edits the title, text or body of an existing lesson. Doesn't change its media, section, schedule or completion rules.

M41.A05.description: Attaches a video, audio, document or other media file to a lesson so learners can view it with the lesson.

M41.A06.description: Moves a lesson into a different section of a course, changing where it appears in the course outline.

M41.A07.description: Sets when a lesson becomes available to learners, such as a fixed date or a delay after enrollment (drip schedule).

M41.A08.description: Defines what a learner must do to finish a lesson, such as viewing it, spending time or passing a quiz.

M41.A09.description: Makes a draft lesson visible to enrolled learners. Opposite of Unpublish lesson.

M41.A10.description: Hides a published lesson from learners and returns it to draft, without deleting it. Opposite of Publish lesson.

M42.A01.description: Enrolls a contact as a learner in a course so they get access to its lessons. Use to sign someone up, not to grant a membership plan.

M42.A02.description: Shows the details of one enrollment, such as learner, course, status, start date and expiry. Use when you already know which enrollment.

M42.A03.description: Finds enrollments by learner, course, status or date. Use to browse many enrollments instead of opening a single one.

M42.A04.description: Sets or changes the date when a learner's course access ends. Use to extend or shorten access without suspending or revoking it.

M42.A05.description: Temporarily blocks a learner's access to a course while keeping their progress. Different from Revoke, which ends the enrollment, and can be undone with Resume.

M42.A06.description: Restores access for a suspended enrollment so the learner can continue where they stopped. Use after Suspend, not for revoked enrollments.

M42.A07.description: Permanently removes a learner's access to a course by ending the enrollment. Stronger than Suspend, which is temporary.

M42.A08.description: Marks a specific lesson as finished for a learner in their enrollment, which updates their progress. Use for single lessons, not for the overall progress report.

M42.A09.description: Reports how far a learner has gotten in a course, including completed lessons and percentage done. Read-only view, unlike Record lesson completion.

M42.A10.description: Issues a certificate to a learner who has finished a course. Use after the course is completed to give them proof of completion.

M43.A01.description: Creates a new community, a discussion space for members, with a name and optional description. Use this to start a brand-new group, not to add a channel inside an existing one.

M43.A02.description: Shows the details of a community, such as its name, description, guidelines, channels and member info. Read-only; use Update guidelines to change rules.

M43.A03.description: Edits the rules or guidelines of a community that members must follow. Changes only the guidelines text, not other community details.

M43.A04.description: Adds a new discussion channel (topic area) inside an existing community so posts can be organized by subject. Different from creating a whole community.

M43.A05.description: Adds a contact as a member of a community so they can read and take part in discussions. Opposite of Leave community.

M43.A06.description: Removes a member from a community so they no longer take part or see its discussions. Opposite of Join community.

M43.A07.description: Publishes a new post or discussion topic in a community channel. Use Reply to community post to respond to an existing post instead.

M43.A08.description: Adds a reply or comment to an existing community post. Differs from Create community post, which starts a new thread.

M43.A09.description: Pins a community post to the top of its channel so members see it first, such as announcements. Does not delete or edit the post.

M43.A10.description: Takes down a community post that was reported for breaking the rules, as part of moderation. Removes the offending content from the community.

M44.A01.description: Creates a new membership plan, an access package that can bundle courses and community access. Use it to define a new tier before granting it to contacts.

M44.A02.description: Retrieves the full details of one membership plan, including its description and entitlements. Use it to view a single plan rather than browse all plans.

M44.A03.description: Lists all available membership plans so you can browse them. Use it to see every plan at once instead of opening a single one.

M44.A04.description: Changes the descriptive text of an existing membership plan. It does not change what the plan includes; use entitlement actions for that.

M44.A05.description: Adds an entitlement to a membership plan, such as access to a course or community, so members of the plan gain that access.

M44.A06.description: Removes an entitlement from a membership plan so members no longer get that course or community access through the plan.

M44.A07.description: Gives a contact a membership under a chosen plan, enabling their access. Use it to enroll someone in a plan; revoking is a separate action.

M44.A08.description: Sets or changes the date when a contact's membership ends. Use it to extend or shorten a membership without revoking it.

M44.A09.description: Removes a contact's membership immediately and ends their plan access. Unlike setting an expiry, it takes effect right away.

M44.A10.description: Checks whether a contact currently has access to a given course or community through their membership. Read-only check that changes nothing.

M45.A01.description: Creates a new review request for a contact, asking them to leave a review. It is saved as unsent; use Send review request to deliver it.

M45.A02.description: Sends an existing review request to the customer so they can leave a review. Differs from Create review request, which only prepares it without delivering.

M45.A03.description: Cancels a review request that has not been sent yet so it will never go out. Cannot be used on requests already delivered.

M45.A04.description: Lists review requests with their status such as unsent, sent or cancelled. Use it to see which customers have been asked for reviews.

M45.A05.description: Records a simulated customer review with rating and text, as if a customer had posted it. Used for testing or logging a review manually.

M45.A06.description: Searches received reviews by keyword, rating, date or reviewer. Returns a list of matches; for one review's full content use Get review details.

M45.A07.description: Shows the full details of a single review, including rating, text, reviewer and any response. Use Search reviews to find it first.

M45.A08.description: Drafts a reply to a customer review and saves it without making it public. Differs from Publish review response, which posts the reply.

M45.A09.description: Publishes a drafted response so it appears publicly under the customer's review. Differs from Draft review response, which only saves the text.

M45.A10.description: Shows summary rating statistics for reviews, such as average rating, total count and distribution by stars.

M46.A01.description: Creates a new business listing profile with the company's name, address, phone and other basics so it can later be published to directories.

M46.A02.description: Opens one business listing and shows its saved name, address, phone, hours and categories. Use to look at a single listing, not to find one.

M46.A03.description: Finds business listings by name, address, city or category. Use when you don't know which listing you need; returns a list of matches.

M46.A04.description: Changes the business name shown on an existing listing. Only the name changes, not the address or phone.

M46.A05.description: Changes the street address, city, state or postal code on a business listing, for example after a move or to fix a mistake.

M46.A06.description: Changes the phone number shown on a business listing. Does not touch the name or address.

M46.A07.description: Sets the days and opening and closing times shown on a listing, including holiday or special hours.

M46.A08.description: Chooses the business categories or industry types a listing appears under in directories, such as restaurant or dentist.

M46.A09.description: Pushes a listing's details out to the simulated directory so it goes live there. Different from checking sync status, which only reports on it.

M46.A10.description: Shows whether a listing's details have reached the simulated directory and match, or if updates are pending or failed.

M47.A01.description: Opens a new support ticket for a customer issue, with subject, details and requester. Use it to log a problem that needs resolution work.

M47.A02.description: Shows the full details of one support ticket, including its subject, status, priority, owner and requester.

M47.A03.description: Finds support tickets by keyword, status, priority, owner or requester. Use it to browse or filter many tickets rather than open a single known one.

M47.A04.description: Assigns a support ticket to a user who will handle it, or changes the current owner to someone else.

M47.A05.description: Sets how urgent a support ticket is, such as low, normal, high or urgent. Does not change its status or owner.

M47.A06.description: Moves a support ticket to a new status such as open, pending, resolved or closed, to show where the work stands.

M47.A07.description: Adds a private note on a ticket visible only to staff, not the customer. Differs from replying to the requester, which sends a message.

M47.A08.description: Sends a reply to the person who raised the ticket, visible to the customer. Differs from an internal note, which stays private.

M47.A09.description: Connects a support ticket to a contact record so the issue appears under that customer, or changes the linked contact.

M47.A10.description: Checks a ticket's service level status: time left to first response or resolution, and whether the deadline is at risk or breached.

M48.A01.description: Invite a new staff member to the account by email; they show as invited until they accept. For customers or prospects use Create contact instead.

M48.A02.description: Show one staff user's profile with roles, status, availability, teams and open task count. For a list of many users use List users.

M48.A03.description: List the staff users working in the account, filtered by role, status, availability, team or name. Not for contacts or leads.

M48.A04.description: Change a staff user's name, email, phone, job title or availability (for example out on leave). Roles and deactivation are separate actions.

M48.A05.description: Give a staff user an additional role such as admin, manager, sales, support, marketing or billing, which determines their permissions. Opposite of Revoke user role.

M48.A06.description: Remove a role from a staff user. They must keep at least one role, and the account must keep one active admin.

M48.A07.description: Deactivate a staff user who left so they can't sign in and leave their teams. Optionally hand their open tasks, leads, contacts and deals to someone else.

M48.A08.description: Restore a deactivated staff user so they can sign in and get work again. Team memberships are not brought back.

M48.A09.description: Show what a staff user is allowed to do and which of their roles grants each permission.

M48.A10.description: Show the audit log of what a staff user changed in the account, newest first, with inclusive dates.

M49.A01.description: Creates a new team of staff users, such as 'EMEA Sales', optionally with starting members, a manager and a way of sharing out work.

M49.A02.description: Shows one team's full details: members with roles and availability, manager and assignment strategy. For all teams at once, use List teams.

M49.A03.description: Lists the teams of staff users (like Sales or Support) with their member ids. Archived teams appear only if requested.

M49.A04.description: Changes the name of a team, and optionally its description. Members and settings stay the same.

M49.A05.description: Adds a staff user to a team so they can receive shared work. Use Assign team manager to make someone the manager.

M49.A06.description: Takes a staff user out of a team. Records they own stay theirs; only future team assignment is affected.

M49.A07.description: Makes a staff user the team's manager, replacing the current one, and adds them as a member if needed.

M49.A08.description: Chooses how new work is shared across a team: round robin (in turn), least busy (fewest open tasks) or manual.

M49.A09.description: Shows each active team member's availability, open and overdue tasks and owned open leads, to find who is free or least busy before assigning work.

M49.A10.description: Archives a team that is no longer used. Members keep their accounts and records; the team just stops receiving work.

M50.A01.description: Creates a new saved report with a name, the metric to measure and starting settings, so it can be run again later. Use Run report for one-off results.

M50.A02.description: Shows the saved settings of one report: its metric, filters, date range and grouping. It does not calculate results; use Run report for that.

M50.A03.description: Lists all saved reports so you can browse or find one by name. Use Get report definition to see the settings of a single report.

M50.A04.description: Changes the filter conditions of a saved report, such as owner, status or source, to narrow the data it covers. Date range and grouping are changed separately.

M50.A05.description: Sets the date range a saved report covers, such as last 30 days or a custom start and end. Differs from Compare report periods, which contrasts two ranges.

M50.A06.description: Sets how report results are grouped or broken down, for example by owner, source, stage or month. Changes the layout only, not the filters.

M50.A07.description: Runs a report and returns the current numbers based on its filters, date range and grouping. Use Export report results to get a downloadable file.

M50.A08.description: Compares a report's results between two periods, such as this month versus last month, showing the change. Differs from Set report date range, which sets one range.

M50.A09.description: Exports a report's results to a downloadable file such as CSV or spreadsheet. Use Run report to just view the numbers.

M50.A10.description: Sets up recurring delivery of a report by email on a schedule, such as weekly or monthly, to chosen recipients. Not for one-off exports.
